subject: Short-hop authorization & regional lockbox — request for operational commitments
messages:
From: security@acme.io
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short-hop / lockbox question for EU workloads

Hi Kimberly,

Quick intro: I’m Lina (security@acme.io), Acme Cloud’s procurement/security lead. We’re moving a batch of EU customer PII into a Redwood-hosted inference pipeline and need to confirm a couple of operational commitments before we finalize the DPA addendum. Specifically: 

- Can Redwood support an explicit “short-hop” window (<= 72 hours) for temporary replication to other regions for operational reasons, with logging and TTL-bound keys?
- If a short-hop occurs, can you guarantee data only touches a defined lockbox VPC (no other external subprocessors) and provide crypto-key custody details (KMS/HSM or key escrows)?
- Please indicate which subprocessors might be involved in that short-hop and whether you have an escrow policy for subprocessor swaps.

We’re on a tight procurement timeline (end of month). If you can point me to any standard playbook or an ops runbook, that’d help.

Thanks,
Lina Torres
Security Lead — Acme Cloud
security@acme.io

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: security@acme.io
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-hop / lockbox question for EU workloads

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear list. We can meet these asks but want to be explicit about the operational guardrails and what we can contractually commit to. High level: 

- Short-hop windows: We support transient cross-region replication for operational resilience and maintenance; our default short-hop tolerance is 48–72 hours depending on the incident class. We can agree to a 72-hour bounded window in a DPA addendum with logging retained for 90 days by default.

- Lockbox VPC & key custody: We can ensure traffic for the short-hop is routed through a customer-scoped lockbox VPC and restrict access to Redwood-managed inference nodes + a named infra partner (see subprocessors). Key management: we offer customer-managed KMS integration for private deployments; for hosted Redwood we use HSM-backed keys and can provide key-rotation and a transient key escrow workflow.

- Subprocessors: I’ll attach the current subprocessors roster and a draft addendum that describes the escrow/swap workflow. We’ll also note which subprocessors are eligible to touch short-hop traffic.

I’m looping in Marissa and Laura to confirm the DPA language we can offer and any procurement/DocuSign artifacts. Jonas — can you add a one-pager for ops runbook links?

Next steps suggested:
1) We share residency-playbook_v2.pdf and subprocessor roster (attached).
2) Legal drafts a narrow DPA addendum with the 72h short-hop window and lockbox commitments.
3) Ops provides the transient-key workflow and acceptance criteria.

If that timeline works, we’ll push a draft to DocuSign within 48 hours.

—Kimberly Park
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, security@acme.io
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-hop / lockbox question for EU workloads

On Mon, 19 Jul 2027 at 09:04, kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
> I’m looping in Marissa and Laura to confirm the DPA language we can offer and any procurement/DocuSign artifacts.

Hi Lina and team — thanks for laying this out. From a legal/commercial perspective we can do a narrowly tailored DPA addendum that includes: 

- A capped transient cross-border processing clause limited to 72 hours with mandatory notification to Acme security within 2 hours of any short-hop initiation.
- A requirement that any short-hop movement is documented in a per-incident runcard (who/why/regions involved) and that audit logs (connection + control plane events) are exported to a customer-accessible log repository for 90 days.
- Lockbox: define the lockbox as a named VPC + network ACLs; subprocessors allowed in that VPC must be enumerated. Any subprocessor swap affecting short-hop eligibility requires 30 days’ notice or immediate escrow activation for critical infra vendors.

Attachment: dpa-addendum-draft.docx (redlined) — this is a starting point. Also attached subprocessor_roster_2027.csv and residency-playbook_v2.pdf for ops detail.

Please review and call out any hard redlines — we’ll keep the language tight to avoid broad ‘sovereignty’ promises beyond the scoped short-hop.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: dpa-addendum-draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
Attachment: subprocessor_roster_2027.csv (text/csv)
Attachment: residency-playbook_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: security@acme.io
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-hop / lockbox question for EU workloads

Hi Lina — quick note from legal: the draft Marissa attached is the narrow approach we prefer. A couple of clarifications before we send to DocuSign: 

1) Documentation & notice: Redwood will provide an incident runcard and an automated notification to the Acme security mailbox when short-hop is triggered. Our SREs will trigger the mechanism, not customer-facing product teams.
2) KMS details: for hosted customers we can provide HSM-backed keys and a signed attestation about key rotation cadence; for private deployments we recommend customer-managed KMS. We cannot, however, escrow customer master keys without a separate escrow agreement (we can offer a brokered escrow for enterprise deals).
3) Subprocessor swaps: 30-day notice for non-critical vendors, immediate notice + escrow activation option for critical infra.

If that’s acceptable, Marissa — please publish the addendum to DocuSign and include the residency-playbook as a reference link.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
General Counsel (Contracts), Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: security@acme.io
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, dpo@datagov.co
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-hop / lockbox question for EU workloads

Thanks — this aligns with what Acme needs. Two quick asks before we sign: 

- Can Redwood provide an ops runbook snippet that lists the exact log fields we’ll receive (timestamps, src/dst regions, key IDs, correlation IDs)?
- We’d like to see a sample signed attestation for the HSM-backed keys (rotation + access controls).

If you can post the runbook snippet to the Drive link and push the addendum to DocuSign, I’ll route to procurement and our DPO. We should be able to complete signing within 3 business days once we have those artifacts.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Lina Torres
Security Lead — Acme Cloud
security@acme.io

Marissa / Laura / Jonas — thanks for the quick responses. Action items I captured: 
1) Marissa: publish dpa-addendum-draft.docx to DocuSign and set signing group to Acme_Security + Acme_Procurement; include a 72-hour short-hop clause and 2-hour notification SLA.
2) Jonas: drop an ops-runbook snippet to the Drive link with the exact log schema and sample attestation (residency-playbook_v2.pdf should reference this).
3) Laura: prepare a short note on the escrow options we can offer for their master keys (brokered escrow pricing to be included).

Target: send DocuSign link and Drive artifacts within 48 hours. I’ll be the primary contact on the procurement thread.

—Kim
